name: Chad

findings.local_actor: Government of Chad (ICT ministry / ADETIC); SOTEL Tchad (state operator)
findings.financier: Export-Import Bank of China (concessional loan, RMB 1.316bn) plus PRC MOFCOM grant (RMB 170m)
findings.summary: Huawei is EPC contractor for Chad's China Exim-financed ICT modernisation project (PMICE): 1,200 km south-east fibre backbone, 50 km N'Djamena loop and SOTEL Tchad upgrade with 200 2G/3G/4G sites and a new core; groundbreaking July 2020.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary), China Development Finance dataset
AidData (William & Mary), China Development Finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Huawei is the equipment vendor/EPC, so pole prc; core-network upgrade of the state operator is the most control-relevant component. Tier 4: loan signed 2019, ratified April 2020, construction started July 2020. No completion confirmed: DCD (Jan 2026) reports a EUR 175m 'Phase I' start covering the same components, unclear whether a relaunch or new phase. USD 189m is the loan at signing and covers the whole bundle including the data centre (TCD-002). OSIRIS 2020 piece cites Huawei as source, so S4. Corroboration of Huawei's role rests on AidData and Ecofin; AidData compiles from secondary reports, so a reviewer may discount independence.

findings.controller: Government of Chad (Centre national des données numériques)
findings.local_actor: Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy; ADETIC; ANSICE
findings.financier: Export-Import Bank of China (part of PMICE loan)
findings.summary: Chad's 500 m2 national digital data centre, built by Huawei under the China-financed PMICE, was nearly complete in January 2025; in February 2026 Techso Group was engaged to audit and certify it before launch.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary), China Development Finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator is the Chadian state, so pole domestic under the building rule; Huawei is builder and China Exim financier. IT equipment inside is likely Huawei-supplied (would be prc under the equipment rule) but not confirmed. Tier 4: built, not yet operational as of Feb 2026. Not an AI campus; no accelerators reported. Digital Business Africa headline mentions fears about China but the page body did not load. Value carried on TCD-001.

findings.summary: Chad's regulator ARCEP signed Starlink's operating authorisation on 13 March 2025 and Starlink launched consumer and business satellite broadband nationwide in early July 2025; the government later complained about its prices and service quality.
findings.analyst_inference: SpaceX controls constellation and terminals, so pole us. Tier 5 as a live commercial service; subscriber numbers unknown. still_current true because a June 2026 report describes the government discussing Starlink pricing and service quality with the company in Washington, implying continued operation. Other reports date a licence approval to Nov 2024; APA gives 13 March 2025 for the signed authorisation.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Public Security; Centre National des Opérations de Vidéosurveillance (CNOV)
findings.summary: Chad's security minister met a Huawei delegation in June 2025 to explore its solutions for an N'Djamena intelligent video-surveillance network across seven zones, run by a national video-surveillance centre; a feasibility study is to precede deployment.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1: exploratory meeting only, no contract or feasibility study reported. Only Alwihda names Huawei; We Are Tech Africa (April 2025) describes the same project with unnamed international experts, so Huawei's role is single-sourced. Pole prc on the named prospective vendor; would be null if another vendor is selected.

silicon.null_reason: no accelerator purchases or deployments surfaced in data-centre, PMICE or AI searches; national data centre not reported as AI-capable

models.null_reason: one search found an AI directorate (Oct 2025), AI strategy work and a May 2026 Washington mission with US firms (InterSystems, Starlink, Cybastion, Vertiv, 19Labs), but no model-provider partnership or sovereign model

research_gaps: Has PMICE (Huawei/China Exim) been completed? Status of the 1,200 km backbone and SOTEL core upgrade; is the EUR 175m 'Phase I' reported by DCD in Jan 2026 the same project relaunched or a new phase, and who finances it?
Who supplies RAN and core for Airtel Tchad and Moov Africa Tchad? Not found; Airtel announced a ~USD 90m network plan in 2025 with no vendor named.
Equipment vendor on the EU/AfDB-financed Trans-Saharan backbone section (contractor CGPS/LORYNE) not named.
Is the national data centre operational yet, who operates it (ADETIC?), and whose IT/cloud stack runs inside it? Digital Business Africa Jan 2025 article on 'fears about China' not readable.
Did the N'Djamena video-surveillance project (CNOV) reach feasibility or contract stage, and with which vendor?
Government-Huawei digital talent agreement (seen in search results, We Are Tech Africa) not opened or coded; training only, but date and terms unverified.
